purpose: Scale from a small high-precision seed to high-recall structural instance candidate generation while preventing missing labels from becoming silent background.

semantic_qa_precondition.rule: Generation is high-recall, but promotion must not violate any semantic hard gate. Review-trigger scenarios remain review-required. Contextual priors can rank or route candidates but cannot create, delete, or relabel an element by themselves.

column: Generate candidates from visible plan-footprint graphics and repeated symbol families.
Use grid alignment, regular spacing, beam framing and cross-level repetition only as contextual evidence.
Never create a column solely from a grid intersection, regular spacing, beam intersection, or because a matching column exists on another level.
Route cross-level disappearance, relocation, offset, or section/symbol change to review; do not force-snap or auto-continue.
beam: Generate candidates from visible framing graphics supported by W/C/other reliable structural designations and drawing context.
Beam-to-column, beam-to-wall and beam-to-beam relationships are contextual evidence only.
Do not silently relabel joists, trusses, bracing, dimensions, grids, leaders, or slab edges as beam.
wall: Start with the two human-confirmed positive pages and regional semantics already confirmed by the project user.
Generate tight axis-aligned source-page boxes only around visible structural wall graphics.
Never use missing column, inside-bay location, perimeter/grid proximity, or wall-like graphics alone as proof of structural-wall status.
Internal shear/core walls remain valid counterexamples to automatic nonstructural classification.
Never infer hidden continuation, bridge openings, or convert paired boundaries to engineering centerlines.

qa_policy.bulk1rule_approval: Allow only after a representative family has been human-reviewed and the rule is stable within the same drafting convention.

scaling_loop: 1. Generate many candidates per in-scope page.
2. Apply semantic hard gates and route review-trigger cases before promotion.
3. Cluster candidates by drafting convention and visual/semantic family.
4. Human-review representative families rather than asking for every instance.
5. Bulk-apply a verified rule only within its verified drafting convention.
6. Route outliers and ambiguous cases back to human QA.
7. Run label-completeness and duplicate gates before training.
8. Train/evaluate only after class coverage and missing-label contamination gates pass.

future_extensibility.note: Future classes require their own versioned ontology/annotation/validation migration; they are not active v0.2 classes.
